ui.app.title: Kun Fayakun
ui.app.tagline: A quiet reflection on creation: verses of the Quran and hadith, each with its source, shown beside what science measures today.
ui.disclaimer: An educational reflection, not tafsir or scientific proof. Interpretations are summarised from cited scholars; for religious guidance, consult a qualified scholar. Science reflects current models and may change.
ui.intro.label: Welcome
ui.intro.sound: There is no music. The film’s sounds come from what it shows: the young universe’s own sound waves until the first light, the Sun’s trembling made audible, rain, wind and the sea. Out in space there is only a low hush, and near silence while a verse is on screen. The explorer plays the wind where there is air, or a suit’s fans where there is none. The speaker at the top turns sound off.

ui.discovery.invite: Each in an orbit: explore its letters
ui.discovery.inline: Explore its letters, read both ways
ui.discovery.title: Letter analysis: kullun fī falakin, “each in an orbit”
ui.discovery.label: Letter analysis: base letters only, diacritics and spaces removed. This is not the Quranic text as written.
ui.discovery.verses: From 21:33 and 36:40, shown in full above.
ui.discovery.tiles: The seven base letters, in reading order from right to left
ui.discovery.same: Read the seven base letters from either end: the sequence is the same.
ui.discovery.conjunction: In 36:40 the phrase begins with the conjunction wa- (“and”), written joined to the first word. It is set aside here, as classical rhetoricians do with a parallel case.
ui.discovery.scope: This holds for these three central words only, not for the whole verse.
ui.discovery.rasm: It is a property of the written base letters (the rasm), not of the pronunciation or the vowelled text.
ui.discovery.classical: Ibn ʿĀshūr (al-Taḥrīr wa-l-Tanwīr, on 21:33) counts it among the text’s embellishments (badīʿ), a figure al-Sakkākī named al-maqlūb al-mustawī.
ui.discovery.closing: A literary beauty of the text, offered for reflection. It is not a proof, a prediction or a numerical sign.
ui.discovery.keys: Arrow keys move the light one letter; Home and End go to either end; Enter plays a reading; P shows the pairs; Esc closes.
ui.discovery.hintTouch: Tap a letter to bring the light to it, or swipe across the letters to move it one letter at a time.
